sections.text: Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys without effort the Bliss which flows from realisation of the Infinite.
He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks on everything with an impartial eye;
यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति।
He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, him shall I never forsake, nor shall he lose Me.

Unlike a car with its users manual, we are born without instructions how to live. We experience life vicissitudes without a so called users manual. The Gita has been described as such a guide.
We had been discussing chapter six, Yoga of Meditation. So far we have seen up to verse 27 that the goal of meditation is to make the mind steady. The mind currently in my present situation is flickering and running away in many, many directions.
And therefore the whole idea of making the mind steady seems very, very difficult for me. So we have seen the practice how to meditate, how to make this mind steady, Choose a place which is conducive, make it a practice every day, make this as a habit, same place, same position, controlling your body from not disturbing you, make it most comfortable, sit down and focus your mind. Now this is where we find ourselves in difficulty focusing the mind on one goal and one target.
We have heard this simile that the mind, when it is like a mind, like a lamp, when there is a wind in the room or in the place where the lamp is placed, the flame flickers. And depending on the nature of the wind, flame may flicker very heavily or may flicker just a little, depending on how much wind there is. The mind works in a similar way.
Depending on my vasanas, depending on the desires in my mind, this mind will be running after many, many thoughts and one thought will lead to the another. Used to say, Im trying to chant Rama and the Rama. The word Rama reminds me of Ramlal who has borrowed money from me.
And then we go on and on and on. But this obviously can be controlled, as we have seen that if you calm down this wind of desires, at least at the time of sitting in the meditation, that you have trained your mind not to think about other things and you focus on that one thought, then mind will be steady. And as we have seen that by a constant practice, the yogi can make his mind steady.
And once that mind becomes steady, he will Recognize the peace within himself from whatever the cause. The restless and the unsteady mind wanders away from that. Let him restrain it and bring it back under the control of the self alone by practice now it is becoming easier for me.
I guess I am speaking for every seeker who is practicing that practice makes man perfect. We have heard this before. We have learned in our life that anything I continue to practice, it becomes easier.
Something which I practice over and over and over again. It reaches a point that there is no effort required. Something like driving a car.
When I was first learning how to drive a car, obviously I had all kinds of problems. And I may have said this before that I used to complain to my cousins who were trying to teach me how to drive a car in Africa. I had gone from India.
I had never driven a car in India. I probably took some lessons in India before I was living for Zambia. And in India it was very easy to get a license.
Nobody even bothered with it. I really knew how to drive, but I got a license now I went to Zambia. And then I really had to drive.
So learning from my cousins how to drive, they kept telling me, Keep your car steady, keep your car steady. And I complained, How can I keep it steady when Im sitting on one side of the car? If the steering wheel was in the center, it would be much easier! But that was just an excuse because I didnt know how to control the car. And then more and more I practice driving the car. It started becoming easier and easier.
And then I reached a point where driving a car requires no efforts. I sit down in the car, put the key in the ignition, can be thinking about every other thing except driving the car. But I will be driving properly in a right lane.
And whatever the appropriate thing I have to do for driving the car. But I do not have to put any more efforts in. Comes automatically and naturally.
As soon as I sit down in the drivers seat, my mind takes over. My subconscious mind takes over how to drive this car. Meditation is like that.
If I practice over and over and over again to steady my mind under one thought and one thought alone. As soon as I sit at the seat of meditation, my mind will know what to do and it will control itself automatically. And Bhagavan says that such a yogi experiences the supreme bliss, that peace which I had been seeking all my life.
And I had been trying to achieve that in many different ways. To acquire things, to make sure everything is secured, my future is secured, my Familys future is secured. However, I never experience that peace in my mind.
Now at the seat of meditation, I can experience the supreme bliss. Bhagavan said, the supreme bliss verily comes to this yogi whose mind is quiet and peaceful. His passions are quietened.
Now he is free from sin. And we have seen the sin is nothing but impurities on my mind. Impurities are the impressions on my mind which makes me think that this I will do and that will make me happy.
Once my mind is steady and is focused on one thought, who I am, what is myself, all these impurities are purified and I achieve that bliss. And the term used is Brahma Bhutam akalmasham. He becomes one with the Brahman all pervading self and he becomes free of all sins.
Continuing in this thought, the next three verses talks about the yogi who has with continued practice has made this as his own nature that the Yunjan Evam Sada Atmanam Yogi Vigada kalmashah. Again we are talking about in Yogi who has become freed from all his sins. Now we sometimes makes an argument that on one hand, the law of karma says that if I have done something, I have to pay for it.
Or if I pay for it, in a sense, if it was a negative act, if it is a positive act, I will get the reward. And then here it says that by meditation I will become free of all sins. How do we reconcile the idea of the law of karma which says you cannot escape from your actions? Here it says just by meditation I can become free from all my sins.
Well, the law of karma simply says that my actions will have equal and appropriate reactions. If Ive done something inappropriate, I will have to pay the consequences. However, the sins here are not the consequences of the actions.
Sins are the impressions on my mind. A negative impression on my mind from any event or experience is a sin. These negative impressions are the ones which are causing me to do more wrong things.
I have seen somebody making money by illegal means. That impressions, that thought or the observation leaves a wrong impression that if I have to make money, it seemed like this is the only way to do it. That negative impression is a sin.
Now that sin will make me act in an inappropriate manner. Then I will also try to achieve the wealth by what I thought was the only way you can achieve wealth by inappropriate means. The wrong impression on the mind made me do the wrong things.
Now I have to face the consequences of those wrong things. However, if I have cleaned up my mind from all these impressions, then Im free of sins. I may still have to face consequences of past actions, but no more wrong actions will be generated from impressions on my mind.
A yogi constantly controlling his mind reaches a level of purification where there are no negative impressions, and therefore there is no cause for him to react inappropriately. So Yunjan Evam Sada Atmanam Yogi Vikatha Kalma Sahar. The Yogi always engaging the mind.
Thus in the practice of yoga, freed from sins, he now Sukena Brahmasp Samsparsam Atyantam Sukham Ashnate. He now easily enjoy that infinite bliss. Because his mind, no matter whatever is happening in his life, in his situations, he is constantly in the thought of that supreme Brahman that he is enjoying that bliss at every moment.
So he has become Brahma sans person. He is in touch with Brahman in all situation and therefore he is experiencing that bliss in all situation. Sukham Atyantam Ashnute and he enjoys this Sukham, this happiness which is infinite.
I have tried in my life all other things, but I never got it. Scripture says that Yogi who meditates and makes his mind steady. Just by that simple act of making the mind steady, he will be in touch with the Brahman.
The supreme reality will be freed from all his limitations. So the yogi has now experienced the supreme bliss. What would be his vision? Sarva Bhutastham Atmanam, Sarva Bhutani Cha Atmani, Ikshate Yoga Yuktatma Sarvatra Samadarshanah.
Now, with his mind harmonized and in touch with the supreme reality, he starts seeing that same reality residing in all beings, and also seeing all beings residing in that supreme reality. We had seen this paradox before in Bhagavad Gita: is Bhagavan within me, or am I in Bhagavan? Is God within me, the limited being, or am I, the limited being, in the God-self which is unlimited? Both are correct. It depends on your viewpoint.
Is the room space in the universal space, or is the universal space in the room? When you see the room space as an individual space, it is nothing but part of the universal space. But when you see the space in the room as part of the universal space, that universal space is in the room. I, the limited being, am in the self of the Bhagavan who is manifesting and pervading everywhere.
But when I look at it from my limited perspective, I see that I, the limited being, have the presence of Bhagavan in me. So I start seeing that he is in all the beings. I also see that all the beings are in that supreme self.
Icsate Yoga Yukta Tatma. Thus the Yogi who is one with the yoga, one, the Yogi who has become one with his Self, he sees this Sarvatra Samadarshanaha everywhere He sees that unity. He sees this presence of the Lord equally in all beings and things.
Same Lord which resides in Me is also residing in everything else that manifests in this world. Such a vision makes this yogi become one with this world, acting as if this world is nothing but his own extension. Yo mam pashyati sarvatra sarvam cha mayi pashyati, tasya aham na pranashyami sa cha me na pranashyati.
Bhagavan now says: Yo mam pashyati sarvatra -- when Lord Krishna in Bhagavad Gita refers to himself in the first person singular, every time that he is not speaking as Devakis son or Yashodas son, but referring to himself as the supreme being pervading everyone. The yogi who sees Me everywhere -- anything I see, I recognize as nothing but Bhagavans manifestation. Sarvam cha mayi pashyati -- I also see Gods presence in everything.
Nothing could have been possible without His presence.

These verses reveal a seeming paradox about sin and karma. If the law of karma says we must face consequences of all actions, how can meditation free us from all sins? The key distinction is that sins here are not the consequences but the impressions (vasanas) that drive future wrong actions. Seeing someone make money illegally creates an impression that this is how wealth is gained. That impression is the sin - it will prompt future wrong action. When meditation purifies these impressions, no new wrong actions arise. You may still face consequences of past actions, but you stop generating new problematic karma.
Verse 29 describes the vision of unity: Sarva-bhuta-stham atmanam sarva-bhutani cha atmani - seeing the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self. This is not poetic metaphor but literal description of realized experience. Just as the space in one room is the same space as in every room, and all rooms exist within infinite space, the consciousness in you is the same consciousness in all beings, and all beings exist within that one consciousness. The apparent diversity is real at one level, yet underlaid by absolute unity.
The beautiful promise of verse 30 - Tasyaham na pranashyami sa cha me na pranashyati - I am never lost to him, nor is he ever lost to Me - assures us that this relationship with the Supreme is mutual. Once you see the Divine everywhere, the Divine is always accessible to you; once the Divine recognizes you as its own, that bond can never break. Today, practice seeing the same life force - the same consciousness - in three very different beings: a family member, a stranger, and a plant or animal. Can you sense the common thread of awareness that animates all three?
